insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Annual Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule / Customer Information Sheet (not provided in excerpt)

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: “At the time of renewal of this Policy, We will provide a Loyalty Bonus of 10% of annual sum insured of immediately preceding policy year subject to a maximum of 100% of the annual sum insured”
great.explanation: A 10% loyalty bonus is added to the annual sum insured at renewal, up to a maximum of 100% of the annual sum insured. This can build your cover up to 2× over time if you stay claim-free.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person.”
good.explanation: The reset sum insured can be used within the same policy year only for future claims that are not related to the illness/disease/injury already claimed for that person. This helps when you have multiple unrelated hospitalizations in a year, but won’t help for repeat admissions for the same condition.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “We will cover the Medical Expenses incurred in respect of Your Domiciliary Hospitalization during the Policy Period… The Domiciliary Hospitalization continues for at least 3 consecutive days…”
good.explanation: Home treatment (domiciliary hospitalization) is covered when it continues for at least 3 consecutive days and meets the policy conditions. This can pay for eligible treatment at home when hospital admission isn’t possible or advisable.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “In consideration of the payment of additional premium to Us, We will cover the expenses incurred on air ambulance services…”
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are covered only if you pay an additional premium for this optional benefit. This can be useful for emergencies, but it is not included by default.

good.name: OPD Cover
good.quote: “In consideration of the payment of additional premium… We will cover you for the Medical Expenses incurred by You in outpatient.”
good.reference: Section C.14 Out Patient Treatment Cover
good.explanation: Outpatient (OPD) medical expenses are covered only if you pay an additional premium for this optional benefit. This can reduce routine healthcare costs, but limits and details depend on the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “Room rent capping shall be applicable to room rent of a hospital room, ICU/ICCU and will be specified in policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet against the benefit.”
bad.explanation: Room rent (including ICU/ICCU) is subject to a cap as per the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet. A room-rent cap can increase your out-of-pocket costs and may also reduce the payable amount for other linked hospital charges.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If the insured chooses a higher room category than the category that is eligible as per terms and conditions of the policy then the insured person shall bear the rateable proportion of the total associated medical expenses.”
bad.reference: Section A.1 Hospitalization Expenses (Inpatient Treatment) + Definitions (Associated Medical Expenses)
bad.explanation: If you choose a room category higher than your eligibility, the insurer applies a rateable (proportionate) deduction on total associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Below are the non-payable items applicable in the policy… 56 GLOVES… 60 MASK…”
bad.reference: Part III (ii) 10 Non Payables (List of Non Payable Items)
bad.explanation: A list of non-payable items applies, including common consumables like gloves and masks. This means you may have to pay these hospital items from your pocket unless covered under a separate add-on/benefit.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “If opted customer will pay the co -pay as per Zone explained below… Zone 1 Nil Nil Nil; Zone 2 10% Nil Nil; Zone 3 15% 5% Nil”
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies if opted, and can be 10% or 15% (and 5% in some cases) depending on the zone. Any co-pay means you must bear part of every admissible claim, increasing out-of-pocket costs.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: “Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… for a period… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet… Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet”
unclear.reference: Section A.3 Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses
unclear.explanation: Pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered for a period that is only stated in the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet. You need to check the schedule to know whether the covered days are adequate (e.g., 30/60/90 days).

unclear.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: “Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… for a period… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet… Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses… as specified against this benefit in the policy schedule/Customer Information Sheet”
unclear.reference: Section A.3 Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses
unclear.explanation: Post-hospitalisation expenses are covered for a period that is only stated in the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet. You need to check the schedule to confirm whether it is 60/90/180 days or more.

unclear.name: PED Waiting Period
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)… shall be excluded until the expiry of specified months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
unclear.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered until completion of the “specified months” of continuous coverage, but the exact duration is not stated here. You must check the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet to know whether it is 24/36/48 months, etc.

unclear.name: Specific Illness Waiting
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of specified months of continuous coverage…”
unclear.reference: Exclusions 3.2 Code-Excl02: Specified disease/procedure waiting period
unclear.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are excluded until completion of the “specified months” of continuous coverage, but the exact duration is not stated here. You must check the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet to know whether it is 24 months or longer.

unclear.name: Initial Waiting Period
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within specified days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident…”
unclear.explanation: Illness claims are excluded for the “specified days” from the first policy commencement date, with an accident exception, but the number of days is not stated here. You must check the Policy Schedule/Customer Information Sheet to confirm whether it is the standard 30 days or more.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
